definition: The space between the last line of defenders and the goalkeeper. A team that defends high leaves it open.
A pass from the defense straight to the forwards, skipping the midfield.
Closing the opponent down near their own box, as soon as they start a move.
Starting a move with short passes from the goalkeeper and the defenders, instead of kicking it long.
match: plays out well from the back

definition: A midfielder who plays in front of the center-backs, shields the defense and helps start moves.
A pass that goes between opposing players and leaves a line of their team behind.
A forward who plays wide, near the touchline, and usually dribbles and crosses.
A defender who plays on the side of the defense and also joins the attack.
The line along each long side of the pitch that marks where the field ends.
Quick short passes between two or three players, such as one-twos, to get past opponents.
A drill where a group passes the ball in a circle while one or two players in the middle try to win it.
Defense, midfield and attack kept close to each other, so there is little space between them.
A move planned and practiced beforehand, usually at corners, free kicks and throw-ins.
Each defender is responsible for one opponent and follows him around the pitch.
Each defender looks after an area of the pitch and marks whoever comes into it.
The set of ideas and behaviors a coach wants the team to show in each phase of play.
The job a coach gives a player, with and without the ball.
When a forward runs back to help the defense after the team loses the ball.
The classic creative midfielder who runs the attack and plays the final pass.
A loose ball that two players contest at the same time, often with a physical challenge.
A contest between two players to head a high ball, as from crosses, corners and long balls.
The club's youth teams, where young players develop before reaching the first team.
Experienced, having played many games and been through many situations.
